title: Keep sounding out apart from word parts
statement: Keep sounding a word out and splitting it into meaningful parts as separate steps: one teaches how the word is said, the other what its parts mean.
detail: Two rulings in a reading course agree. The course's rulebook puts syllables first and the meaning-part split second, as a separate, later move, because meaningful parts and spoken parts are different things and must never share one tile (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-6/distilled/04-CONTENT-AUTHORING.md`, lines 407-410). A later ruling on the vocabulary card's sound-it-out clips says that step teaches pronunciation, not partitioning, with every chunk pronounced as it sounds inside the word, while the printed meaning parts are a different step and stay as they are (`grade3-reading/.claude/skills/sound-out-respell/SKILL.md`, lines 12-14).

evidence.quote: the beat teaches pronunciation, not partitioning — every chunk is pronounced exactly as it sounds inside that word. The printed morphemes (morph.parts, the word-parts stage) are a different beat and stay as they are.
the morpheme split is a separate, later move. "Morphemes are meaningful elements, syllables are spoken parts" — the two must never be conflated on one tile.
